channel.title: Daily Recap — 🚦Start Up
channel.description: What happened in 🚦Start Up, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: Cloudflare acquires Deno to improve its Workers programming model
item.description:
Cloudflare has acquired Deno — the company co-founded by Node.js creator Ryan Dahl — to strengthen the programming model behind Cloudflare Workers. TechCrunch and Techmeme both covered the deal and what it means for the edge-computing stack.

Sources:

  • Cloudflare acquires Deno to improve its Workers programming model
  • Cloudflare acquires Deno, co-founded by Node.js creator Ryan Dahl

item.title: Inside Anthropic: revenue math questioned, agents filing visas, and how GOP ties ended a safety standoff
item.description:
Techmeme rounds up a busy Anthropic news day: differing calculations of Anthropic and OpenAI revenue are under the microscope, the company's AI agents reportedly submitted 20 visa applications via a State Department form, and a look at how co-founder Tom Brown used GOP ties to end a June standoff over model safety.

Sources:

  • A look at differing revenue calculations of Anthropic and OpenAI
  • Sources: Anthropic's AI agents submitted 20 visa applications via a form on the US State Department
  • How Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown used GOP ties to end a June standoff over model safety

item.title: TikTok US still coordinates with global org; Senate investigates hyperscalers
item.description:
Current and former employees say TikTok US still coordinates closely with the global TikTok organization, while a Senate investigation led by Warren, Van Hollen, and Blumenthal says some hyperscalers are under scrutiny.

item.title: Walmart's warehouse automation push hits trouble; laptop production drifts back to China
item.description:
A look at Walmart's troubled effort to automate its ~200 US warehouses with partners like Symbotic, plus new data showing laptop production share outside China falling from 24% to 21% as PC makers retrench.

Sources:

  • A look at Walmart's troubled push to automate its ~200 US warehouses
  • Laptop production share outside China is expected to fall from 24% in 2025 to 21% in 2026

item.title: Publishers feed books to AI without author consent; Synopsys explores China AI lab partnerships
item.description:
Dozens of staff at HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster, and Hachette say publishers are feeding books to AI without author consent. Separately, chip design leader Synopsys says it's exploring partnerships with Chinese AI labs.

  • Chip design software leader Synopsys says it is exploring partnerships with Chinese AI labs

item.title: Firmus IPO collapsed in 48 hours; Xbox hardware sales hit an all-time low
item.description:
Sources detail how Firmus' IPO collapsed in 48 hours after US fund managers balked at its $30B valuation. Meanwhile Circana data shows US Xbox unit sales fell 33% year-over-year to an all-time low through August, while PS5 sales held up.

Sources:

  • Sources detail how Firmus' IPO collapsed in 48 hours after US fund managers deemed its $30B valuation
  • Circana: US Xbox unit sales fell 33% YoY to an all-time low in 2026 through August

item.title: Startup watch: Petra Power's data-center energy play; 3 days to TechCrunch Disrupt
item.description:
Petra Power looks to modernize energy for data centers and defense vehicles. Also: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is 3 days out with a preview of startups to watch, TechCrunch rounds up AI agents that live in your text messages, and a profile of secretive solo investor Zach Frankel.
